Solution: the assertion is now three, each with its own budget — the row is waited for by subject (`/^add notes/`), then its accessible name (`add notes +3 -0`), then `aria-expanded`. add.issue.comment.md:
Solution: added a `halfyear` scope between `month` and `year`. Two calls worth recording:

- **180 days, not 182.5.** Six of the `month` scope (30 days) rather than half of `year` (365), so paging back by a half-year lands on the same boundaries the month scope steps on.
- **Labelled "6 months".** Every other scope's button label is its id capitalized; `Halfyear` is not a word anyone wants, so `scopeButtonLabel` special-cases this one. The pager reads "Last 180 days", matching "Last 30 days" / "Last 365 days".

No axis work needed — `chooseSegmentUnit` picks off the duration, so 180 days gets month segments on its own. PR #270.

add.issue.comment.md:
Solution: `96f16f65` (PR #271). Went with the eslint rule rather than the pre-commit fallback — flat config takes a local plugin inline, so it is ~40 lines in `source/scripts/eslint-rules.mjs`, and `npm run lint:err` already runs in both the pre-push gate and CI. Rule: no character below U+0020 in the source text other than tab and newline; escapes are ASCII in the file and untouched.

It found two live NULs on its first run, in `epiq-api.test.ts` lines 977 and 989 — deliberate hostile-payload inputs someone wrote as raw bytes rather than escapes. That file has been binary to git ever since; escaping them restores its diff and makes the test's intent readable. Its 94 tests pass unchanged.

Worth recording because it is the ticket's own point made twice: before writing the rule I swept the repo with `grep -rlP` for control characters and it reported nothing — because grep could not see into the very file that had them.

Tested in `source/test/eslint-rules.test.ts` through `Linter`: a raw NUL, several in one file, escapes, tab/newline. The fixtures build their control characters with `String.fromCharCode` rather than literals, so the test file does not become the thing it is testing for.
